question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=1+2{e}^{x+1}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3).$
question.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(3).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(3)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(3) & =x \\ f(x) & =3 \\ 1+2{e}^{x+1} & =3 \\ 2{e}^{x+1} & =2 \\ {e}^{x+1} & =1 \\ x+1 & =0 \\ x & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(3)=-1.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(-1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =1+2{e}^{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2{e}^{0} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
